During the week he was enrolled in the program, Mr. Donnelly mentioned that he planned to help a friend who sells cars on the side. However, he never indicated that he intended to leave the program. On Monday, July 20, Mr. Donnelly did not report to the program and did not call to notify staff of his absence. DiYoung attempted to contact him but was unable to reach him.

Later that week, when it was time for Mr. Donnelly to pick up his pay card, he contacted DiYoung and explained that he had started helping his friend with the car business. He also informed staff that he would not be returning to the program.

processed_notes.note_text:
Purpose of the Meeting

The purpose of today’s meeting was to strengthen Rodney’s motivation toward his 90-day goals, identify barriers to success, reinforce his personal strengths, and develop measurable action steps that support long-term recovery and successful community re-entry.

Primary 90-Day Goal

Rodney identified maintaining his sobriety as his highest priority.

He stated that sobriety is the foundation of every other goal in his life.

“If I lose that, I lose everything else.”

⸻

Client Strengths

Rodney demonstrated several protective factors throughout the session:

* Strong insight into addiction and recovery
* Accepts personal responsibility for past choices
* Strong spiritual beliefs
* Connected to a sponsor and recovery community
* Motivated to rebuild family relationships
* Open to accountability
* Demonstrates honesty regarding barriers
* Willing to take recovery one day at a time

⸻

Discussion Summary

Recovery

Rodney shared that maintaining sobriety remains his greatest accomplishment and his number one priority. He recognizes that employment, transportation, housing, and family restoration all depend upon remaining sober.

He discussed avoiding people, places, and situations associated with past substance use by limiting conversations and immediately removing himself from high-risk environments.

⸻

Emotional Regulation

Rodney acknowledged that reacting impulsively when feeling disrespected has created significant problems throughout his life.

He identified a healthier response:

* Stop
* Think
* Respond instead of react

He recognizes that changing his thinking before acting is essential to preventing negative consequences.

⸻

Transportation

Transportation remains Rodney’s largest barrier.

Current plan includes:

* Working at a local car lot
* Hoping employer provides transportation
* Mother available to transport him to work if necessary

Rodney also acknowledged the need to eventually resolve:

* Outstanding fines
* Habitual offender status
* Driver’s license reinstatement

⸻

Housing

Housing is currently stable.

Rodney is living with his mother and identified this as a positive source of support while rebuilding his life.

⸻

Employment

Rodney is optimistic about employment opportunities.

He expressed appreciation for beginning with manageable work rather than placing excessive pressure on himself.

He understands financial stability will come gradually through consistency.

⸻

Recovery Supports

Rodney identified multiple recovery supports:

* Church
* 12-Step meetings
* Sponsor
* Positive mentors
* Recovery peers

He described these relationships as essential because they model the lifestyle he hopes to maintain.

⸻

Thinking Patterns

Rodney demonstrated healthy cognitive restructuring by recognizing:

* He cannot control other people.
* Doing the right thing does not guarantee easy circumstances.
* Acceptance is necessary when facing situations beyond his control.
* Daily decisions determine long-term outcomes.

He referenced the Serenity Prayer as a guide for managing frustration.

⸻

Accountability

Rodney stated he benefits from multiple accountability partners rather than relying on one individual.

He expressed that regular check-ins provide encouragement, motivation, and opportunities for self-reflection without feeling judged.

⸻

Family

Rodney became visibly encouraged discussing reconnecting with his daughter and grandson.

His daughter recently reestablished contact after several years.

He identified restoring this relationship as one of his strongest motivations to remain sober and consistent.

⸻

Financial Stability

Rodney reported:

* No bank account currently
* Interested in opening a checking/savings account
* Wants to learn healthy money management
* Understands financial responsibility must be developed gradually

⸻

Education

Rodney is actively completing Home Depot Pro training and reported nearly completing the electrical certification module.

⸻

Motivational Interviewing Techniques Utilized

Throughout the session, the case manager utilized:

* Open-ended questions
* Reflective listening
* Affirmations
* Goal clarification
* Values exploration
* Developing discrepancy between past behaviors and future goals
* Eliciting change talk
* Supporting self-efficacy
* Collaborative planning

⸻

Change Talk Identified

Rodney expressed several statements indicating readiness for change:

* “Everything comes from my sobriety.”
* “I have to stop and think.”
* “One thing at a time.”
* “I want to stay consistent.”
* “I don’t even want to be around that old person anymore.”
* “When the student is ready, the teacher will appear.”

These statements demonstrate increased commitment to personal growth and sustained recovery.

⸻

Goals Before Next Meeting

Rodney agreed to focus on the following commitments over the next week:

1. Maintain sobriety through daily recovery practices.
2. Attend scheduled 12-Step meetings and remain connected with his sponsor.
3. Continue avoiding high-risk people, places, and situations.
4. Complete the Home Depot Pro electrical training.
5. Continue pursuing reliable transportation.
6. Strengthen his relationship with his daughter and spend meaningful time with his grandson.
7. Practice stopping to think before reacting when faced with frustration or perceived disrespect.

⸻

Case Manager Observations

Rodney presented as engaged, honest, reflective, and receptive throughout today’s meeting. He demonstrated increased insight into the relationship between his thoughts, behaviors, and recovery outcomes. He consistently identified sobriety as the foundation for all future goals and showed realistic expectations regarding the pace of his re-entry process.

Rodney appears internally motivated, connected to meaningful recovery supports, and committed to taking gradual, measurable steps toward long-term stability. Continued weekly motivational interviewing sessions, accountability check-ins, and reinforcement of his recovery supports are expected to strengthen his confidence, consistency, and successful community reintegration.

Rodney expressed a high level of motivation to participate in the structured program. He shared that he has been searching for help to better understand the decisions that have led to negative consequences in his past, stating that “going back to prison isn’t even an option.” Rodney reported that he is willing to do whatever is necessary to succeed. He lives approximately five minutes from the center with his Mom and has reliable transportation through his girlfriend, whom he identified as his primary support. Rodney stated that he is tired of the direction his life has taken and is committed to giving himself a second chance by taking advantage of the opportunities available through the program to become a better version of himself. After enrolling Rodney, I will be looking forward to monitoring his engagement, how he reinforce his own strengths and motivation, and support him in achieving his personal goals while utilizing his support system throughout the program.
